bugs.title: Image-to-text recognition fails to load the Tesseract JavaScript chunk
bugs.error: Text recognition failed: Loading chunk node_modules_pnpm_tesseract_js_7_0_0_node_modules_tesseract_js_src_index_js failed. (error: http://127.0.0.1:4300/node_modules_pnpm_tesseract_js_7_0_0_node_modules_tesseract_js_src_index_js.js)

findings: OcrEngineService previously dynamically imported tesseract.js when recognition first ran, creating an extra package-path chunk inside an already lazy feature.
The installed Tesseract version is 7.0.0; its package entry point is src/index.js.
The reported development server at 127.0.0.1:4300 was unreachable during investigation.

Starting the development server initially failed because Node.js v24.11.0 does not meet the installed Angular CLI requirement: v22.22.3, v24.15.0, or v26.0.0 minimum on the corresponding release line.
A supported Node.js v26.12.0 runtime is available at C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe.

The normal web development configuration is independently blocked by missing @mobile-gallery-view source. Existing desktop routing allowed development-server OCR validation without changing that unrelated code.
Forcing the old Tesseract chunk URL to return 404 reproduced the exact reported error before the fix. After the fix, OCR succeeds with that URL still blocked.
investigation.rootCause: An unnecessary nested dynamic import made recognition depend on an additional package-path Tesseract chunk. Missing that chunk causes the reported failure. The reason it was missing in the original browser session could not be established.

resolution.summary: Bundle typed Tesseract exports with the dynamically imported OCR window, eliminating the second dynamic package chunk while keeping OCR outside initial application chunks.
verification: 22/22 targeted OCR and document-tab tests passed using installed Edge.
Desktop production and extension builds passed.
Both build graphs contain Tesseract only in lazy OCR chunk 302, not in initial chunks or a separate tesseract-js chunk.
Real development-server OCR recognized HELLO OCR 2026 at 95% confidence with the old chunk URL forced to 404.
Repeated recognition succeeded with one worker load; OCR resources were absent before opening the window.

bugs.notes: Reload existing browser tabs after restarting the development server so they use the updated chunk graph. The unrelated missing @mobile-gallery-view dependency was not changed.
